sources.citation: Chemorion, Diphus Chosefu. 2008. Translating Jonah's narration and poetry into Sabaot: towards a participatory approach to Bible translation (PABT). DTh thesis, Stellenbosch University (handle 10019.1/1094)
sources.note: §4.4.3.2 pp. 94-95: Sabaot orthography (SIL/Sabaot Language Committee, approved 1988) 'has very special features for marking grammatical tones'; 13 consonants, 20 vowels citing Kipkirich & Larsen 2006:2-4, 18-19. Nothing on stress (the only 'stress' hit is Nord's general text-analysis model).

sources.citation: Lodge, Ken. 1995. Kalenjin phonology and morphology. Lingua 96: 29-43 (held on file under catalog nand1266)
sources.note: Tugen dialect; lists 'Mount Elgon speakers: Sapiny, Kany, Terik, Pok, Pong'om' as a Kalenjin grouping; ATR harmony only; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Hartell, Rhonda L. (ed.). 1993. Alphabets of Africa. Dakar: UNESCO/SIL, p. 188 'Kenya: Sabaot (Southern Nilotic)' (Rosetta Project scan)
sources.note: Phoneme/orthography chart; 'Tone: Tone markers before the word shows grammatical tone distinctions' (subject vs non-subject noun tone, indefinite subject, 2nd vs 3rd person, future vs negative non-past, emphatic); stress not mentioned.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE, Sabaot (saba1262) inventory 'sabaot (AA 812)' = Hartell 1993 Alphabets of Africa
sources.note: 31-segment inventory derived from the Alphabets of Africa page; no tone or stress information.

sources.citation: Rottland 1982, pp. 22-23 (Elgon-Zweig: Kony, Pok, Bong'om, Terik) and pp. 20-22 (Sapiny; Nandi, Kipsikiis, Keyo, Tuken) — Rosetta Project excerpt pages
sources.note: Ethnographic/geographic sections only (names, self-designations, settlement); nothing on stress or tone.
